1717:         private void EmitAssignmentExpression(BoundAssignmentOperator assignmentOperator, bool used)
1718:         {
1719:             if (TryEmitAssignmentInPlace(assignmentOperator, used))
1720:             {
1721:                 return;
1722:             }
1723: 
1724:             // Assignment expression codegen has the following parts:
1725:             //
1726:             // * PreRHS: We need to emit instructions before the load of the right hand side if:
1727:             //   - If the left hand side is a ref local or ref formal parameter and the right hand 
1728:             //     side is a value then we must put the ref on the stack early so that we can store 
1729:             //     indirectly into it.
1730:             //   - If the left hand side is an array slot then we must evaluate the array and indices
1731:             //     before we evaluate the right hand side. We ensure that the array and indices are 
1732:             //     on the stack when the store is executed.
1733:             //   - Similarly, if the left hand side is a non-static field then its receiver must be
1734:             //     evaluated before the right hand side.
1735:             //
1736:             // * RHS: There are three possible ways to do an assignment with respect to "refness", 
1737:             //   and all are found in the lowering of:
1738:             //
1739:             //   N().s += 10;
1740:             //
1741:             //   That expression is realized as 
1742:             //
1743:             //   ref int addr = ref N().s;   // Assign a ref on the right hand side to the left hand side.
1744:             //   int sum = addr + 10;        // No refs at all; assign directly to sum.
1745:             //   addr = sum;                 // Assigns indirectly through the address.
1746:             //
1747:             //   - If we are in the first case then assignmentOperator.RefKind is Ref and the left hand side is a 
1748:             //     ref local temporary. We simply assign the ref on the RHS to the storage on the LHS with no indirection.
1749:             //
1750:             //   - If we are in the second case then nothing is ref; we have a value on one side an a local on the other.
1751:             //     Again, there is no indirection.
1752:             // 
1753:             //   - If we are in the third case then we have a ref on the left and a value on the right. We must compute the
1754:             //     value of the right hand side and then store it into the left hand side.
1755:             //
1756:             // * Duplication: The result of an assignment operation is the value that was assigned. It is possible that 
1757:             //   later codegen is expecting this value to be on the stack when we're done here. This is controlled by
1758:             //   the "used" formal parameter. There are two possible cases:
1759:             //   - If the preamble put stuff on the stack for the usage of the store, then we must not put an extra copy
1760:             //     of the right hand side value on the stack; that will be between the value and the stuff needed to 
1761:             //     do the storage. In that case we put the right hand side value in a temporary and restore it later.
1762:             //   - Otherwise we can just do a dup instruction; there's nothing before the dup on the stack that we'll need.
1763:             // 
1764:             // * Storage: Either direct or indirect, depending. See the RHS section above for details.
1765:             // 
1766:             // * Post-storage: If we stashed away the duplicated value in the temporary, we need to restore it back to the stack.
1767: 
1768:             bool lhsUsesStack = EmitAssignmentPreamble(assignmentOperator);
1769:             EmitAssignmentValue(assignmentOperator);
1770:             LocalDefinition temp = EmitAssignmentDuplication(assignmentOperator, used, lhsUsesStack);
1771:             EmitStore(assignmentOperator);
1772:             EmitAssignmentPostfix(temp);
1773:         }
